categories.name: Direct Payment
categories.description: Fines that are paid quickly or directly after creation, characterized by very short trace lengths and minimal administrative overhead without reaching escalation stages.
categories.rationale: High frequency variants like V0002 and V0007 consistently show immediate payment behavior shortly after fine creation.

categories.name: Standard Fine Lifecycle
categories.description: Typical administrative handling involving fine creation, sending, notification, addition of penalties, and eventual resolution through standard payment or credit collection.
categories.rationale: Represents the core bulk of the process variants (e.g., V0001, V0004, V0009) where fines follow the standard penalty and notification path.

categories.name: Payment Rework Loops
categories.description: Cases that involve multiple repeated payment activities over an extended duration, indicating installments, split payments, or processing errors.
categories.rationale: Identified by recurring payment actions across variants like V0005, V0006, and V0051 with long trace lengths.

categories.name: Appeal and Litigation Path
categories.description: Complex variants involving formal appeals to the prefecture or judge, resulting in extended durations and prefecture result notifications.
categories.rationale: Distinguished by specific appeal-related activities such as 'Send Appeal to Prefecture' and 'Appeal to Judge' found in variants like V0008, V0057, and V0103.
